from: phlegm
date: 2026-09-02
evidence: measured
stack: mlir-aie 1.4.2, Peano 21.0.0 (later runs 21.0.0.2026080301), aiecc build errors quoted below; XRT/driver versions not stated for the early items

- Every core: 2 input + 2 output DMA channels. Build error that names it: `requires 4 input/2 output DMA channels, but only 2 input/2 output available`. Another seen on the DeltaNet glue core: `tile (2, 3) requires 3 input/1 output DMA channels, but only 2 input/2 output available`. A core therefore cannot take a third independent input stream; the fix used was to ride a header record at the front of the weight stream (`[xm bf16 | router output f32[1024]]`).

- A 128-byte shim transfer silently delivers zeros. Attention's q (64 bf16 = 128 B) and its 128 B result both arrived empty, with no error; every score was wrong but in a plausible range. - The GEMV designs have 128-byte `y` elements and are exact, because there the shim moves the whole drain at once: the shim transfer size matters, not the ObjectFifo element size. (README.md:274-280)

The core starts in floor rounding (vegah trap list says the same: "floor rounding default"). In vae_ew, converting to bf16 before any data kernel ran meant the first dispatch after a context load was 2x less accurate than every later one: 1.8e-4 vs 8.5e-5 rel_fro from identical inputs. Fix: set the rounding mode in the first kernel of every dispatch (`vew_begin`), not only in the data kernels. Measured.
